PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: character-jesus-the-harrower-primary-appearance
Workflow profile: 4X3 (4:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Character guard: the row alone defines identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, hair, scars, costume, wounds, pose, and carried objects. Never turn a non-Jesus character into a Jesus lookalike.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain; explicitly requested ivory-linen/blood material behavior only; explicitly requested golden luminous-VFX behavior only; explicitly requested production-sheet spacing/readability only.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
JESUS CHRIST — PRIMARY APPEARANCE: FOUR-VIEW IDENTITY, ANATOMY, COSTUME, AND CONTINUITY REFERENCE.

Create a four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet showing the same person in frontal three-quarter portrait, full-body, side profile, and rear-head/costume view. Lock facial identity, age, ethnicity, hairline, complete crown and rear hair, costume construction, body proportions, hands, scars, wounds, and carried props across every panel. One face exists only on the front of the head. Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet for Jesus the Harrower, the same continuous living man locked across every panel for the biblical epic JESUS: THE HARROWING OF HELL. Age appearance approximately thirty years. Height roughly five feet ten inches. Athletic muscular build that is strong and human, never bodybuilder-exaggerated, with broad shoulders, defined but natural forearms and hands, solid core under the robe, and calm grounded stance. Mediterranean olive skin with warm subsurface scatter, fine natural pores, light weather at the cheeks from outdoor life, and a short soft beard of the same dark brown-black as the hair, closely kept and continuous around the jaw without ornamental styling.

Face identity must remain identical in every view where the face is visible: long oval structure, high thoughtful brow, straight Mediterranean nose, full but quiet mouth set in absolute calm certainty beyond anger and beyond triumph, strong but gentle jaw. Dark brown eyes hold infinite compassion and absolute authority at once; irises deep amber-brown with wet catchlights from divine gold key light; lids relaxed, gaze steady and unhurried. Expression is deliberate presence, never frantic, never cruel, never smirking. One face exists only on the front of the head; the rear-head panel shows only hair and costume, never a second face, never a rear visage, never any facial features on the back of the skull.

Hair continuity is critical: long dark brown to near-black hair with complete crown coverage and full rear-head density, mid-back length when free, natural waves with weight and gravity, individual strands catching ethereal gold rim light. Hairline natural and continuous over the temples and crown; rear view must show thick complete coverage at the nape and crown with no bald patch, no undercut modern styling, no ponytail hardware. Optional faint dried blood traces at the hairline and upper forehead from the crown of thorns, subtle and residual rather than fresh streams, matching the same blood map used across the production.

Blood continuity map locked across all panels where skin is visible: fresh-to-recent blood staining both wrists at the nail-wound sites, dark crimson dried edges with still-wet cores that have soaked into the white linen cuffs; a side wound on the right flank of the torso where the spear pierced, blood soaking a vertical-to-diagonal stain through the robe at the ribs and hip; optional faint forehead blood as noted. Wound anatomy remains human and photoreal, never grotesque spectacle. Hands are anatomically correct, clean construction with visible nail-wound centers on both palms/wrists area, fingers long and capable, ready to rest on a hilt or open against iron.

Costume construction locked: simple white linen ankle-length robe of handwoven period fabric, soft vertical folds, slight translucency at edges where backlit by divine gold, fabric weight that hangs with gravity. Material shows real linen weave, slight uneven handspun texture, dust and ash grit along the lower hem from descent through hell’s shaft, and the blood stain map at both wrists and the right side wound as fixed geography—not random red smears. Leather cord belt cinched at the natural waist in a simple functional knot, rough vegetable-tanned leather with warm brown tone and slight fray at the ends. Footwear: rough leather sandals with simple straps across the foot and around the ankle, dusty soles, period construction only. No jewelry, no modern hardware, no logos, no embroidered symbols that read as text.

Carried prop continuity: the Sword of Light held in the right hand in the full-body and portrait-adjacent views where a prop is shown—simple leather-wrapped hilt of dark worn leather cord, modest crossguard without ornament, blade not metal but pure concentrated golden divine radiance that cuts darkness like cloth, soft volumetric glow along the edge, no readable runes, no modern sword silhouettes. When the sword is present it emits warm ethereal gold that rims the knuckles and robe sleeve; when a panel isolates costume without the weapon, hands remain empty but the same hand anatomy and wounds remain.

Panel layout and locking: (1) Frontal three-quarter portrait from mid-chest up, face primary, divine golden key light from above-front slightly camera-left, soft fill from cold blue hell-torch bounce at very low intensity so skin still reads warm, shallow depth of field on the eyes. (2) Full-body standing figure, upright posture of measured certainty, weight evenly distributed, robe hanging to ankles over sandals, sword of light held relaxed but ready at the side or lightly raised, head level, presence commanding space without effort. (3) True side profile, locked nose-to-chin silhouette, hair volume over the ear and down the neck, blood at wrist visible if arm is forward, single facial plane only. (4) Rear-head and full costume back view: complete hair crown and nape, robe back construction, belt knot or cord ends, sandal heels, no face on the back of the head under any circumstance.

Lighting and color for the sheet: primary key is ethereal gold and pure white divine radiance approximately warm-gold with high-key god-ray quality, secondary environmental bounce of deep crimson and cold blue torch light at low fill so the figure remains readable as the light-bearer inside hell’s fortress palette. Soft volumetric atmosphere, faint ash motes in air, physically coherent shadows. Skin subsurface warm olive; linen bright but stained; leather matte and real; sword-blade light soft-edged and holy rather than neon. Color grade locks to ethereal golds, warm amber, pure white divine highlights, deep crimson shadows, and restrained cold blue rim only as hell context—never modern teal-orange grading.

Camera and production language: photorealistic live-action biblical epic production reference, as if photographed on a real set for a prestige 2.39:1 feature, sharp anatomical fidelity, consistent scale between panels, matching body proportions, matching hair density, matching wound placement, matching robe damage and stain map. Soft cinematic portrait lighting on the face, full-body panel lit for costume readability, no illustration look, no anime, no CGI cartoon, no plastic skin. Sacred reverent tone appropriate to the Harrowing: the Living One who died and lives forevermore, descending in golden light through the shaft with calm certainty, white robe blood-marked from the cross, keys of death and Hades held as quiet absolute fact rather than spectacle.

Hard constraints repeated for model lock: one face only on the front of the head; exact blood map at both wrists, side wound, and optional forehead; same white linen robe damage and stain geography; same long dark hair with complete crown and rear coverage; same Mediterranean olive identity approximately age thirty, height five-ten, athletic not exaggerated; same leather cord belt and rough leather sandals; same simple leather-wrapped sword of pure golden light when shown; no modern objects, no clocks, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, no captions, no written or graphical elements of any kind on the image.
